title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 5 Lesson 2: Rough Inclined Plane Single Limit custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A block of mass $4\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough plane inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $\mu = 0.4$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 40\text{ N}$), calculate the normal reaction $R$ and the maximum possible static friction force $F_{\max}$.

A crate rests on a rough plane whose inclination $\theta$ to the horizontal is gradually increased. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.75$. Find the critical angle of inclination $\theta_c$ at which the crate is on the point of sliding down the plane under its own weight alone.

A particle of mass $5\text{ kg}$ ($W = 50\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with $\mu = 0.2$. A force $P$ acts up the line of greatest slope. Calculate the minimum value of $P$ required to prevent the particle from slipping down the slope.

A sled of mass $20\text{ kg}$ ($W = 200\text{ N}$) is pulled up a rough slope inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal at constant speed by a cable parallel to the slope. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.15$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the cable correct to 3 significant figures.

A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ ($W = 60\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.6$. No external force is applied. Calculate the actual frictional force $F_f$ acting on the block.

A block of mass $2\text{ kg}$ ($W = 20\text{ N}$) is held on a rough plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal by a horizontal force $P$ directed into the plane. The coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. If the block is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping down the plane, calculate $P$.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $m = 26\text{ kg}$ ($W = 260\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{5}{12}$ (so $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$). The coefficient of friction between the crate and the plane is $\mu = 0.25$. A rope pulls the crate with force $P$ acting up the line of greatest slope. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the normal reaction $R$ and the maximum possible frictional force $F_{\max}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the force $P_1$ required to pull the crate up the plane at constant speed, and determine the minimum holding force $P_0$ required to prevent the crate from sliding down the plane.

questions.prompt: A parcel of mass $8\text{ kg}$ ($W = 80\text{ N}$) is on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A force of magnitude $65\text{ N}$ acting up the line of greatest slope places the parcel in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping UP the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the plane, and find the magnitude of the frictional force $F$ acting on the parcel.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the parcel and the plane correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m = 12\text{ kg}$ ($W = 120\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $24^\circ$ to the horizontal. A pulling force of magnitude $65\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $36^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope. The block is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding up the plane. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane, calculate the friction force $F$ and the normal reaction $R$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the block and the plane correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $m_A = 6\text{ kg}$ ($W_A = 60\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between block $A$ and the plane is $\mu = 0.3$. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ runs up the line of greatest slope, passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline, and supports a vertically hanging mass $B$ of mass $m_B$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction on block $A$ and find the minimum mass $m_B$ needed to prevent block $A$ from sliding down the incline.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum mass $m_B$ that can be suspended without causing block $A$ to slide up the incline.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $m = 10\text{ kg}$ ($W = 100\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.6$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.8$. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is $\mu = 0.5$. A horizontal force of magnitude $P$ directed towards the plane pushes against the block. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving perpendicular to the inclined plane, express the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the block is in limiting equilibrium on the point of sliding down the plane, calculate the minimum horizontal force $P_{\min}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If the horizontal force $P$ is increased until the block is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping UP the plane, calculate the maximum horizontal force $P_{\max}$.

questions.prompt: A heavy packing case of mass $M = 50\text{ kg}$ ($W = 500\text{ N}$) rests on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the case and the plane is $\mu = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 0.577$. A worker pulls the case with tension $T$ at an angle $\theta$ above the line of greatest slope ($0^\circ \leqslant \theta < 60^\circ$). Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Form the equilibrium equations along and perpendicular to the slope when the case is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping up the plane, and show that $T(\cos\theta + \mu\sin\theta) = 500(\sin 30^\circ + \mu\cos 30^\circ)$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given $\mu = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, show that the tension $T$ is minimized when $\theta = 30^\circ$, and calculate this minimum pulling tension $T_{\min}$ and the corresponding normal reaction $R$.

questions.prompt: Two blocks $P$ and $Q$, of masses $m_P = 4\text{ kg}$ and $m_Q = 6\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light rigid rod parallel to the line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Block $P$ is higher up the slope than block $Q$. The coefficients of friction between the plane and the blocks are $\mu_P = 0.2$ and $\mu_Q = 0.5$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum possible friction forces $F_{P,\max}$ and $F_{Q,\max}$ that can act on blocks $P$ and $Q$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that the system of two blocks cannot remain in equilibrium on the slope under gravity alone, and explain whether the connecting rod is in tension or compression.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A holding force $F_{\text{hold}}$ is applied to block $Q$ acting up the line of greatest slope. Calculate the minimum value of $F_{\text{hold}}$ to maintain equilibrium, and find the thrust (compressive force) in the rod under this minimum holding force.
